newsitem.title: FRANCE: Popularity of France's Chirac, Juppe slipping.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of France's Chirac, Juppe slipping.

text.p: The popularity of French Gaullist President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe slipped in an opinion poll released on Tuesday but conducted before Chirac announced a snap parliamentary election.
The BVA poll, for the weekly Paris-Match, rated Chirac's popularity at 35 percent, down from 39 percent a month earlier.
The percentage of people with a poor opinion of the president rose to 57 percent from 55 percent in the same period, according to the poll of 935 adults.

The poll was conducted from April 17 to 19 amid speculation that Chirac would call an early election. He announced on Monday that he was dissolving the National Assembly and calling an election on May 25 with a runoff round on June 1.
Juppe's popularity dropped to 25 percent from 29 percent while the percentage of people with a poor opinion of him rose to 66 from 63 percent.

The percentage of people satisfied with the way the ruling centre-right coalition runs France was steady at 20 percent while those dissatisfied dropped one percentage point to 75 percent, the poll showed.
Chirac and Juppe rated 10th and 18th respectively among the public's preferred politicians.
Topping the list was Socialist former European Commission president Jacques Delors who has withdrawn from active politics.
